entry: Japanese actress. She is widely considered one of the greatest Japanese film actresses. She is best known for films by [[Yasujirō Ozu]], including *Late Spring* (1949), *[[Tokyo Story]]* (1953) and *Tokyo Twilight* (1957), and she also worked extensively with director Mikio Naruse. She debuted at 15, in 1935, with Nikkatsu Studios, and first gained prominence in the 1937 German-Japanese co-production *Die Tochter des Samurai*. After World War II she starred in the first postwar film of [[Akira Kurosawa]], *No Regrets for Our Youth* (1946). In most of her films, especially those by Ozu and Naruse, she played typical Japanese women as daughters, wives or mothers. Hara never married and was nicknamed "the Eternal Virgin" in Japan. She quit acting in 1963, the year Ozu died, and lived in seclusion in Kamakura, refusing interviews, until she died of pneumonia.

Largest city on the [[Crimea|Crimean peninsula]] and a major port on the [[Black Sea]]. Founded in 1783, it has been a major base for Russia's Black Sea Fleet and was a closed city during the [[Cold War]]. Its harbors have made it a naval base, and its mild winters and warm summers have made it a seaside resort popular with visitors from former Soviet republics. It is internationally recognized as part of [[Ukraine]]. Russia has controlled the city since February 2014 and annexed Crimea in March 2014; Ukraine regards this as occupation. Most residents are ethnic Russians.

Classic puzzle in [[Graph theory|graph theory]]. It asks whether a walk can cross each of the seven bridges of [[Königsberg]], a city in Prussia (now [[Kaliningrad]], [[Russia]]), exactly once. In 1736 [[Leonhard Euler]] proved that no such walk exists. He showed that the route within each land mass is irrelevant and reduced the city to a graph of land masses and bridges. All four land masses were touched by an odd number of bridges, so the walk is impossible. His analysis laid the foundations of graph theory and foreshadowed [[Topology|topology]].

Japanese epic *jidaigeki* film directed by [[Akira Kurosawa]], co-written with Shinobu Hashimoto and Hideo Oguni. It tells of a village of peasants who hire seven [[Samurai|samurai]] to defend them from bandits who will return after the harvest. Starring [[Toshiro Mifune]] and Takashi Shimura, the film was released in Japan on April 26, 1954, with a runtime of 207 minutes. Kurosawa won the Silver Lion for direction at the Venice Film Festival, and [[Columbia Pictures]] distributed it in the United States in 1956. It was nominated for two [[Academy Awards]] and three BAFTAs but won none. Its story was remade in the 1960 Western *The Magnificent Seven*, and the film is considered one of the greatest ever made.

headword: Seven Wonders of the Ancient World
sort_key: seven wonders of the ancient world
entry: Traditional list of seven notable structures of classical antiquity. It was established in the 1572 publication *Octo Mundi Miracula*, though the first known list of seven dates from the 2nd–1st century BC and ancient lists differ. It names the [[Great Pyramid of Giza]], the [[Colossus of Rhodes]], the Lighthouse of Alexandria, the Mausoleum at Halicarnassus, the Temple of Artemis at Ephesus, the Statue of Zeus at Olympia and the Hanging Gardens of Babylon. Only the Great Pyramid, by far the oldest, remains. Remains of the lighthouse, temple and mausoleum survive in situ or in museums, and scholars debate whether the Hanging Gardens existed at all. Earlier and later lists by [[Herodotus]] and Callimachus survive only as references.

Global conflict fought mainly in [[Europe]], [[North America]] and India, 1756–1763. Great Britain and [[Prussia]] fought France and Austria, joined by Portugal, Spain, Sweden, Russia and Saxony. Its North American phase began in 1754 with a clash over the [[Ohio River]] valley, where [[George Washington]] led Virginia militia that ambushed a small French force. In Europe, Austria sought to recover [[Silesia]], but the Treaty of Hubertusburg (1763) confirmed Prussian occupation of Silesia and its status as a great power. Under the Treaty of Paris (1763), France lost its North American possessions and Britain established commercial dominance in India, while Havana and Manila, taken from Spain, were returned.

Set of major vices in Christian teaching. Also called capital or cardinal vices, the seven deadly sins are not listed in the [[Bible]] but developed within early Christian tradition. In the standard list used by the [[Catholic Church]], they are wrath, greed, pride, envy, sloth, lust and gluttony. The classification into seven originated with [[Tertullian]] and was continued by Evagrius Ponticus. In AD 590, [[Pope Gregory I]] revised the list into the form that has become common. Since then the idea has influenced religious and philosophical thought, fine art, and popular media such as literature, film and television.

Adventist Christian denomination distinguished by its observance of Saturday as the [[Sabbath]] and its emphasis on the imminent [[Second Coming]] of [[Jesus]]. It grew out of the Millerite movement in the United States and was formally established in 1863. Co-founder Ellen G. White's writings remain highly regarded. Its theology shares evangelical teachings such as the [[Trinity]] and the infallibility of Scripture, and it advocates [[Vegetarianism|vegetarianism]] and emphasizes Jewish dietary law. The church is governed by a General Conference and reported over 24 million baptized members as of 2016, with a missionary presence in more than 215 countries and territories. It operates over 7,500 schools, numerous hospitals and publishing houses, and the Adventist Development and Relief Agency (ADRA).

Capital of [[Andalusia]] and of Seville province, in southern [[Spain]] (pop., 2025: 688,714). It lies on the lower Guadalquivir River in the southwest of the [[Iberian Peninsula]]. Its port, about 80 km from the Atlantic Ocean, is the only river harbor in Spain. Founded by the Romans as Hispalis, the city was ruled by Muslim dynasties after 711 and was incorporated into the Crown of Castile in 1248. As the gateway of the [[Spanish Empire]]'s trans-Atlantic trade, managed from the Casa de Contratación, Seville became one of the largest cities in [[Western Europe]] in the 16th century. Trade later moved gradually to the Bay of Cádiz as drought conditions deteriorated in the Guadalquivir. Its Alcázar palace complex, cathedral and General Archive of the Indies form a [[World Heritage Site|UNESCO World Heritage Site]].

Process of removing contaminants from municipal wastewater. It aims to produce an effluent suitable for discharge to the environment or for reuse, thereby preventing [[Water pollution|water pollution]] from raw sewage. Secondary treatment uses aerobic or anaerobic biological processes to reduce organic matter, measured as biological oxygen demand. Tertiary treatment adds polishing and nutrient removal, reducing [[Nitrogen|nitrogen]] and [[Phosphorus|phosphorus]] and disinfecting against [[Pathogen|pathogenic organisms]]. A quaternary step can remove micropollutants such as pharmaceuticals, as implemented at full scale in Sweden. High-income countries treat about 74% of their sewage, but developing countries treat an average of just 4.2%. Treatment is part of [[Sanitation|sanitation]].

Craft of fastening textiles together with a needle and thread. One of the oldest textile arts, it originated in the Paleolithic era, when early humans in Europe and Asia made fur and leather garments with bone, antler or ivory needles and thread of sinew or catgut. For thousands of years all sewing was done by hand, and before the 19th century most of it repaired clothing. Decorative [[Embroidery|embroidery]] was valued in many cultures, and its stitches spread along trade routes such as the [[Silk Road]]. The [[Sewing machine|sewing machine]], invented in the 19th century, mechanized stitching and enabled mass garment production in the 20th century. Hand sewing remains common in high-quality tailoring, haute couture and custom dressmaking.

Machine used to stitch fabric and other materials together with [[Thread (textiles)|thread]]. Invented during the first [[Industrial Revolution]] to reduce manual sewing in clothing companies, it greatly improved efficiency in the [[Clothing industry|clothing industry]]. The first machine is generally credited to Englishman Thomas Saint, who designed one in 1790 but probably never built it. The first practical, widely used machine was invented by the French tailor Barthélemy Thimonnier, whose machine sewed straight seams with a chain stitch. American inventor Elias Howe patented a lockstitch machine in 1846. Home machines are designed for one person to sew individual items, while industrial machines are larger, faster and more specialized. Early machines were powered by a flywheel handle or a foot treadle, and electric machines came later.

English punk rock band formed in London in 1975. The band initiated the [[Punk rock|punk]] movement in the United Kingdom. Its sole studio album, *Never Mind the Bollocks, Here's the Sex Pistols* (1977), was a UK number one. The single "God Save the Queen" (1977) was banned by the [[BBC]] and nearly every independent British radio station. Vocalist Johnny Rotten announced the break-up in January 1978,. Sid Vicious died of a heroin overdose in 1979. Inducted into the [[Rock and Roll Hall of Fame]] in 2006, the band reformed in 2024 with guest vocalist Frank Carter.

American romantic comedy-drama television series made for [[HBO]]. Created by Darren Star and based on Candace Bushnell's newspaper column and 1996 book, it follows four women in [[New York City]]: Carrie Bradshaw (played by [[Sarah Jessica Parker]]), Samantha Jones, Charlotte York and Miranda Hobbes. It ran for six seasons and 94 episodes, from June 1998 to February 2004, and won seven Primetime Emmy Awards. Two feature films followed in 2008 and 2010. A sequel series, *And Just Like That...*, premiered on HBO Max in 2021 without Kim Cattrall, who played Samantha.

Instruction on issues relating to human sexuality. It covers human sexual anatomy, sexual activity, [[Birth control|birth control]], safe sex, reproductive rights, emotional relationships and the [[Age of consent|age of consent]]. Comprehensive sexuality education covers all of these issues, whereas abstinence-only education focuses solely on promoting sexual abstinence and is often favored in socially conservative regions, including parts of the [[United States]]. Programs may be delivered in schools, through public health campaigns, or by parents. Many governments see it as beneficial to provide education before or at the beginning of [[Puberty|puberty]], to improve public health, limit the spread of [[Sexually transmitted infection|sexually transmitted infections]] and avoid teenage pregnancy. In the late 19th century, progressive educators introduced sex education in North American schools as "social hygiene". The first sex education curriculum in Singapore, from 1966 to 1973, emphasized birth control as a way to avoid overpopulation.

Businesses providing sex-related products, services or adult entertainment. Also called the sex trade, it includes direct services such as [[Prostitution|prostitution]] and strip clubs, and goods such as [[Pornography|pornography]], adult magazines and [[Sex toy|sex toys]]. It employs millions of people worldwide, mainly women, from sex workers to support personnel. Prostitution may take place in a [[Brothel|brothel]], a client's hotel room, a parked car or on the street. The term appears to have arisen in the 1970s, and "industry" can be misleading, as many enterprises are artisanal and unconnected.

Part of an organism involved in sexual reproduction. Sex organs produce and transport gametes, facilitate fertilization and support the development and birth of offspring. They are found in many animal and plant species and together form the reproductive system. The Latin term genitalia describes the externally visible sex organs. In humans and other mammals, the primary sex organs are the ovaries in females and the [[Testicle|testicles]] in males, which generate gametes and produce most primary hormones. Secondary sex organs include the [[Clitoris|clitoris]], oviducts and [[Vagina|vagina]] in females, and the epididymides and [[Penis|penis]] in males. In [[Flowering plant|flowering plants]], stamens produce [[Pollen|pollen]], while pistils produce ovules and receive pollen for fertilization.

Positioning of the bodies that people use during sexual intercourse or other sexual activity. Sexual acts are generally described by the positions the participants adopt, and sex positions commonly involve non-penetrative activities. The three broad, overlapping categories of sexual activity are vaginal sex, anal sex and oral sex, and a fourth, manual sex, involves stimulation by the hands. Early guides include a Greco-Roman sex manual by Philaenis of Samos and the [[Kama Sutra]]. [[Alfred Kinsey]] categorized six primary positions. In the [[Missionary position|missionary position]], the partners face each other. Some authors argue that the number of positions is essentially limitless.

Person or character widely regarded as sexually attractive. The term was first used in the 1910s and 1920s for emerging film stars. Silent actor [[Rudolph Valentino]], whose role in *The Sheik* (1921) established him as a major star, is regarded as the first screen sex symbol. In the 1950s the "bad boy" image was epitomized by [[James Dean]] and [[Marlon Brando]], and the blonde bombshell by [[Marilyn Monroe]]. Until the 1950s a sex symbol was seen as a sexual ideal; in the 1960s it came to symbolize the emancipation of sexuality with the [[Sexual revolution]].

Object or device used primarily to facilitate sexual pleasure. Many, such as the [[Dildo|dildo]] and [[Vibrator (sex toy)|vibrator]], resemble human genitals and may be vibrating or non-vibrating. The term can also include BDSM apparatus and sex furniture such as sex swings, but not [[Birth control|birth control]], pornography or [[Condom|condoms]]. They are sold mainly at sex shops and online, and also in pharmacies and department stores. Erotic electrostimulation uses electricity to stimulate nerve endings, a principle borrowed from medical TENS machines, which were widely available by the mid-1970s.

Doubly reflecting navigation instrument that measures the angle between two visible objects. Its primary use is to measure the altitude of a celestial body above the horizon, such as the [[Sun]] at noon or [[Polaris]] at night, to estimate [[Latitude|latitude]]. Measuring the lunar distance between the [[Moon]] and another body gives [[Greenwich Mean Time]] and hence [[Longitude|longitude]]. Its frame is a sector of about one-sixth of a circle (60°), hence the name from the Latin for "one sixth". Unlike the backstaff, it allows direct observation of stars, and because it does not depend on electricity or GPS, it is a practical back-up for ships. The principle was first implemented around 1731 by John Hadley and Thomas Godfrey. In 1922, Carlos Viegas Gago Coutinho adapted it for aeronautical navigation.

Field of research, health care and social activism concerned with the health of the reproductive system and sexual well-being at all stages of life. It is more commonly defined as sexual and reproductive health and rights, which encompasses individual agency to make choices about sexual and reproductive lives. The [[World Health Organization]] (WHO) has a working definition of sexual health (2006) as a state of physical, emotional, mental and social well-being in relation to sexuality, not merely the absence of disease, dysfunction or infirmity. The WHO assessed in 2008 that reproductive and sexual ill-health accounts for 20% of the global burden of ill-health for women and 14% for men. The Guttmacher–Lancet Commission warned that almost all of the 4.3 billion people of reproductive age worldwide will have inadequate sexual and reproductive health services over their lives.

Physiological and psychological changes in preparation for sexual intercourse, or in response to sexual stimuli. In males, arousal leads to erection and pre-ejaculate. In females, sexual tissues such as the nipples, [[Clitoris|clitoris]] and vaginal walls become engorged, the cervix changes, and vaginal lubrication occurs. Arousal has several stages and may not lead to sexual activity. Touch and hormone fluctuations can influence it, and sufficient stimulation in the right context can lead to [[Orgasm|orgasm]]. Stimuli may be somatosensory, visual or olfactory. Arousal dependent on objects is called [[Sexual fetishism|sexual fetishism]] or, in some instances, a [[Paraphilia|paraphilia]].

Sexual abuse in which one person intentionally touches another sexually without consent, or coerces or forces a sexual act. It is a form of sexual violence that includes [[Child sexual abuse|child sexual abuse]], groping, [[Rape|rape]], forced kissing, drug-facilitated assault and sexual torture. Generally, it is defined as unwanted sexual contact, and in most U.S. states it occurs when there is a lack of [[Consent|consent]]. Consent must be given by adults who are not incapacitated and may be withdrawn at any time. Child sexual abuse can cause depression, [[Post-traumatic stress disorder|post-traumatic stress disorder]], [[Anxiety|anxiety]] and an increased risk of re-victimization in adulthood. Most sexual abuse offenders are acquainted with their victims. Approximately 15 to 25 percent of women and 5 to 15 percent of men were sexually abused as children, and such abuse is often not reported.

Attraction on the basis of sexual desire, or the quality of arousing such interest. Sexual attractiveness is a factor in sexual selection or mate choice, and it may be enhanced by body odor, [[Pheromone|sex pheromones]], clothing, perfume or hairstyle. It is influenced by individual genetic, psychological and cultural factors, and depends both on the person attracting and on the criteria of the person attracted. Attractiveness is largely subjective, depending on the observer's interest, perception and sexual orientation. [[Asexuality|Asexuality]] refers to those who do not experience sexual attraction. The ovulatory shift hypothesis proposes that female sexual behavior and desire vary across the [[Menstrual cycle|menstrual cycle]]. The ability of physical qualities to create sexual interest underlies their use in advertising, film and modeling.
